suggestions.title: Measure your waist circumference
suggestions.description: Fat around the middle raises heart and metabolic risk, even at a healthy weight. Aim for a waist under half your height. Add your waist measurement.
suggestions.reason: Fat around the middle is linked to heart and metabolic risk. Waist-to-height ratio can flag risk that a healthy BMI misses; the AACE 2025 and NICE guidelines suggest keeping it under 0.5.

references.label: Ashwell 2012 – WHtR better than BMI for cardiometabolic risk (Obes Rev)

suggestions.title: Daily protein target: 72g
suggestions.description: Based on your ideal body weight of 60.0 kg, aim for 72g of protein daily. This supports muscle maintenance and metabolic health.
suggestions.reason: Higher protein intake supports muscle maintenance, metabolic health, and healthy aging. Research shows that 1.2g per kg of ideal body weight optimises muscle protein synthesis. If kidney function is reduced (eGFR below 45), a lower target of 1.0g/kg is recommended to reduce kidney workload.

references.label: Naghshi 2020 – Protein & all-cause mortality (BMJ meta-analysis)
Morton 2018 – Protein & muscle gains (Br J Sports Med meta-analysis)
Jäger 2017 – ISSN position stand: protein & exercise
Tagawa 2021 – Protein dose-response for muscle mass (Nutr Rev)

suggestions.title: Reduce sodium intake
suggestions.description: Aim for less than 1,500mg of sodium daily. Most excess sodium comes from processed foods. Reducing sodium can help lower blood pressure.
suggestions.reason:
Excess sodium raises blood pressure by increasing fluid retention. The ACC/AHA guidelines recommend an ideal sodium intake of less than 1,500mg per day for most adults. Meta-analyses confirm that reducing sodium intake produces meaningful blood pressure reductions, with greater benefit in those who already have elevated blood pressure.

A potassium-enriched salt substitute (75% sodium chloride, 25% potassium chloride) lowered stroke, major cardiovascular events and death in the SSaSS trial, in people in rural China with a past stroke or older adults with high blood pressure. The 2025 AHA/ACC guideline says these substitutes can be useful, except in kidney disease or with medicines that reduce potassium excretion. NICE advises against them for people with diabetes and pregnant women too. So the plan says not to use one if you are pregnant, have kidney disease or diabetes, have been told to limit potassium, or take a potassium-sparing diuretic, a potassium supplement, an ACE inhibitor or an ARB, unless your doctor agrees, and shows the suggestion only with a current eGFR of 45 or more. NICE also advises against them for older people.

Huang 2020 – Dietary sodium reduction & BP (BMJ)
Charchar 2023 – ISH lifestyle management of hypertension
Whelton 2017 – ACC/AHA Blood Pressure Guideline (Hypertension)
Neal 2021 – Salt substitution and cardiovascular events: SSaSS trial (NEJM)
Gulati 2025 – 2025 AHA/ACC High Blood Pressure Guideline-at-a-Glance (JACC)
NICE NG136 – Hypertension in adults: diagnosis and management

suggestions.title: Maximize fiber intake
suggestions.description: Aim for 25-35g of fiber daily from whole grains, fruits, and vegetables. Increase gradually to avoid discomfort. If you have IBS or IBD, discuss appropriate fiber levels with your doctor.
suggestions.reason: Dietary fibre may lower cardiovascular risk through several mechanisms: reducing cholesterol absorption, improving blood sugar control, and supporting a healthy gut microbiome. Large cohort studies link the highest fibre intakes with roughly 15–30% lower rates of heart disease, stroke and death than the lowest, and trials show fibre lowers cholesterol and blood pressure.

references.label: Reynolds 2019 – Carbohydrate quality & human health (Lancet meta-analyses)
Hartley 2016 – Fibre may lower cholesterol and diastolic blood pressure (Cochrane Review)

suggestions.title: Foods that lower cholesterol
suggestions.description: Specific foods can lower LDL cholesterol: oats, walnuts, almonds, ground flaxseed, edamame, and replacing butter with extra-virgin olive oil. If you don't have IBS or IBD, beans, lentils, chickpeas, and mixed vegetables are also great options. Psyllium husk is a soluble fibre that is well-tolerated even with IBS or IBD; discuss with your doctor whether it fits your routine.
suggestions.reason: These foods lower LDL cholesterol through complementary mechanisms: beta-glucan (oats) and soluble fibre (psyllium, flaxseed) bind bile acids, reducing cholesterol reabsorption. Nuts (walnuts, almonds) provide unsaturated fats that improve the LDL-to-HDL ratio. Replacing saturated fat (butter) with monounsaturated fat (extra-virgin olive oil) directly lowers LDL. Soy protein (edamame) modestly reduces LDL when replacing animal protein. Combined, these dietary changes can reduce LDL cholesterol by 15–25%.

references.label: Jenkins 2011 – Portfolio Diet effect on LDL cholesterol (JAMA)
Sabaté 2010 – Nut consumption and blood lipid levels (Arch Intern Med)
Wei 2009 – Psyllium fibre lowers cholesterol: meta-analysis (Eur J Clin Nutr)

suggestions.title: Regular cardio and resistance training
suggestions.description: Aim for at least 150 minutes of moderate cardio, or 75 vigorous, or a mix (vigorous minutes count double), plus 2-3 resistance training sessions per week. This combination supports cardiovascular health, muscle mass, and metabolic function.
suggestions.reason: The World Health Organization (2020) and the Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans recommend at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity, or at least 75 minutes of vigorous activity, or a mix of the two (each vigorous minute counts as about two moderate minutes), plus muscle-strengthening activity on 2 or more days a week. Large studies (PURE, 130,000 people across 17 countries) show that higher physical activity reduces all-cause mortality regardless of income level or country. Cardiorespiratory fitness is one of the strongest predictors of how long people live.

references.label: Bull 2020 – WHO guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour (Br J Sports Med)
Piercy 2018 – Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans (JAMA)
Lear 2017 – Physical activity & mortality in 130,000 people (Lancet PURE)
Kodama 2009 – Cardiorespiratory fitness & mortality (JAMA)

suggestions.title: Prioritize quality sleep
suggestions.description: Aim for 7-9 hours of sleep per night. Maintain a consistent sleep schedule, limit screens before bed, and keep your bedroom cool and dark.
suggestions.reason: Consistent sleep of 7–9 hours per night is essential for cardiovascular health, immune function, and cognitive performance. A large meta-analysis of over 1.3 million participants found that both short sleep (<6 hours) and long sleep (>8–9 hours) are associated with significantly increased mortality risk.

references.label: Cappuccio 2010 – Sleep duration & all-cause mortality: meta-analysis (Sleep)

suggestions.title: Consider a GLP-1 medication
suggestions.description: With a BMI of 25.2 and elevated blood pressure, you may benefit from discussing Tirzepatide (preferred) or Semaglutide with your doctor, alongside diet, exercise and sleep. These medications support weight management and metabolic health.
suggestions.reason:
GLP-1 receptor agonists like tirzepatide and semaglutide have been shown in large randomised trials to produce significant, sustained weight loss alongside improvements in blood sugar, blood pressure, and triglycerides. Tirzepatide is preferred due to its dual GIP/GLP-1 mechanism, which may provide greater weight loss. These medications work best alongside diet, exercise, and sleep optimisation.

This plan raises these medications earlier than guidelines do. Guidelines consider them at a BMI above 30, or above 27 with a weight-related condition, after 3–6 months of lifestyle change. This plan suggests discussing them at a BMI of 30 or more, above 28 unless your waist is in the healthy range, and from 25 when a marker is raised: HbA1c, blood pressure, triglycerides, cholesterol or waist size. No guideline supports these lower BMI thresholds, and a doctor may not agree to prescribe below the licensed ones. The cholesterol lines (ApoB 130 mg/dL, LDL-C 160 mg/dL, non-HDL-C 190 mg/dL or more) are the risk-enhancing levels in the 2018 AHA/ACC cholesterol guideline, which uses them to guide statin decisions, not weight medication.

references.label: Wilding 2021 – Semaglutide for overweight/obesity: STEP 1 trial (NEJM)
Wilding 2022 – Weight regain after semaglutide withdrawal (Diabetes Obes Metab)
Grundy 2018 – AHA/ACC cholesterol guideline: risk-enhancing factors (Circulation)

suggestions.title: HbA1c in normal range
suggestions.description: Your HbA1c of 38 mmol/mol is in the normal range. Continue healthy habits to maintain this.
suggestions.reason: A normal HbA1c (below 5.7% / below 38.8 mmol/mol) indicates healthy blood sugar control over the past 2–3 months. Maintaining this through diet, exercise, and healthy weight reduces your long-term risk of diabetes.

references.label: ADA – Standards of Medical Care in Diabetes

suggestions.title: Stage 1 hypertension
suggestions.description:
Your BP of 128/82 mmHg indicates stage 1 hypertension. Target is <120/80.

Key lifestyle measures: reduce sodium intake (<1,500mg/day), exercise regularly (150+ min/week), and prioritize quality sleep (7-9 hours).

Weight loss is one of the most effective ways to lower blood pressure. Even a 5% reduction can make a meaningful difference. GLP-1 medications (tirzepatide, semaglutide) can assist with both weight loss and blood pressure reduction.
suggestions.reason:
Stage 1 hypertension (130–139 systolic or 80–89 diastolic mmHg) is the point at which blood pressure starts to cause meaningful cardiovascular damage over time. Lifestyle measures are the first-line treatment: reduce sodium, increase potassium-rich foods, exercise regularly, prioritise sleep, and manage weight.

Some doctors target <120/80 mmHg for adults under 65. The SPRINT trial showed that targeting <120 mmHg (vs <140 mmHg) reduced cardiovascular events by 25% and all-cause mortality by 27%. The ESPRIT trial extended these findings to a broader population including those with diabetes.

references.label: Charchar 2023 – ISH lifestyle management of hypertension
Filippini 2021 – Sodium reduction & blood pressure (Circulation)
Huang 2020 – Dietary sodium reduction & BP (BMJ)
SPRINT 2015 – Intensive BP lowering <120 mmHg (NEJM)
Liu 2024 – ESPRIT: intensive BP lowering incl. diabetes (Lancet)

suggestions.title: Consider adding Ezetimibe
suggestions.description: Your LDL-c is 3.6 mmol/L; the treatment target is below 1.4 mmol/L. Discuss adding Ezetimibe 10mg with your doctor. Not studied enough in pregnancy: talk to your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to be. If you become pregnant, most people should stop their statin: talk to your doctor. If you are planning a pregnancy, NICE advises stopping 3 months before trying to conceive.
suggestions.reason:
Ezetimibe works differently from statins — it blocks cholesterol absorption in the intestine. Adding ezetimibe to a statin typically lowers LDL by an additional 15–20%. Recent evidence shows that starting ezetimibe early alongside a statin produces better cardiovascular outcomes than adding it later.

If a statin is not tolerated, this plan suggests a PCSK9 inhibitor first, because the outcome evidence for ezetimibe on its own is limited, and ezetimibe after it if your level is still above target.

Its US label says there are not enough data on ezetimibe in pregnancy to judge the risk.

references.label: 2026 ACC/AHA Dyslipidemia Guideline (JACC)
Mach 2020 – ESC/EAS Dyslipidaemia Guidelines (Eur Heart J)
Leosdottir 2025 – Early vs late ezetimibe initiation (JACC)
FDA label – Zetia (ezetimibe), 8.1 Pregnancy: insufficient data to evaluate risk (DailyMed)

suggestions.title: Start colorectal cancer screening
suggestions.description: Dr Brad recommends starting colorectal screening at 35, because colorectal cancer has become more common in younger adults. The official guideline (American Cancer Society) starts at 45. Dr Brad suggests a FIT test every year until 55, then a colonoscopy every 10 years. Discuss with your doctor.
suggestions.reason: Dr Brad recommends starting colorectal screening at age 35, because colorectal cancer in adults under 50 has become more common in many countries since the mid-1990s. This is his recommendation, not the official guideline: the American Cancer Society recommends starting at 45 for people at average risk and continuing through 75. Dr Brad suggests a stool test (FIT) every year until 55, then a colonoscopy every 10 years. This order is his suggestion; the American Cancer Society lists FIT every year and colonoscopy every 10 years, among other tests, as equal options from 45. After a positive test and a colonoscopy, follow the repeat interval in your colonoscopy report, which depends on what was found; if the report gave none, Dr Brad suggests repeating the colonoscopy every 3 years. This default is his recommendation, not a guideline figure.

references.label: American Cancer Society – Screening Guidelines
Siegel 2019 – Rising early-onset colorectal cancer globally (Gut)
Wolf 2018 – Colorectal cancer screening for average-risk adults: 2018 guideline update from the American Cancer Society (CA Cancer J Clin)

suggestions.title: Start breast cancer screening
suggestions.description: Mammography is optional at your age (40–44). Discuss with your doctor.
suggestions.reason: Mammography screening reduces breast cancer mortality by detecting cancers early, when treatment is most effective. The ACS recommends annual mammograms starting at age 45 (optional from 40). The benefits and appropriate frequency should be discussed with your doctor based on your individual risk.

references.label: American Cancer Society – Screening Guidelines

suggestions.title: Start cervical cancer screening
suggestions.description: HPV testing every 5 years (preferred) or Pap test every 3 years is recommended. Discuss with your doctor.
suggestions.reason: Cervical screening (HPV testing or Pap smear) detects precancerous changes caused by human papillomavirus. Catching these changes early prevents cervical cancer from developing. HPV testing every 5 years is now preferred over Pap smears every 3 years due to higher sensitivity.

references.label: American Cancer Society – Screening Guidelines

suggestions.title: Micronutrient base
suggestions.description: A meta-analysis of three COSMOS trial sub-studies (2024) found that a daily multivitamin improved global cognition and episodic memory in older adults. This suggests broad micronutrient support may benefit brain health alongside filling common dietary gaps. The WHO's 2026 dementia guideline recommends against vitamin B, vitamin E, omega-3 and multivitamin-mineral supplements to reduce the risk of cognitive decline and dementia in people without a diagnosed deficiency, a strong recommendation based on moderate-certainty evidence. It kept its earlier recommendation without reassessing supplements, and did not cite the COSMOS trials. If you take warfarin (Coumadin, Marevan) or another vitamin K antagonist, check with your doctor or anticoagulation clinic before starting or stopping vitamin K2, because it can change your INR.

references.label: Vyas 2024 – Multivitamin & cognition: COSMOS-Clinic + meta-analysis of 3 COSMOS sub-studies (Am J Clin Nutr)
Baker 2023 – Multivitamin & cognitive function: COSMOS-Mind trial (Alzheimers Dement)
WHO 2026 – Risk reduction of cognitive decline and dementia: guidelines, 2nd edition
Theuwissen 2013 – Low-dose vitamin K2 (MK-7) and oral anticoagulant stability (J Thromb Haemost)

suggestions.title: Creatine
suggestions.description: One of the most-studied supplements: a meta-analysis found creatine (3–5 g/day) significantly increases muscle strength and lean mass with resistance training. There is also an interesting signal that it may help memory, another possible benefit; formal reviews are mixed, with the clearest benefit in older adults.

references.label: Kreider 2017 – ISSN position stand: creatine safety & efficacy (J Int Soc Sports Nutr)
Avgerinos 2018 – Creatine & cognition: systematic review (Exp Gerontol)
Prokopidis 2023 – Creatine & memory: meta-analysis of RCTs (Nutr Rev)
Prokopidis 2023 – Authors' reply and reanalysis: memory benefit only in older adults (Nutr Rev)
Xu 2024 – Creatine & cognition in adults: meta-analysis of 16 RCTs (Front Nutr)
EFSA 2024 – Creatine & cognitive function: health claim not substantiated (EFSA J)

suggestions.title: Collagen peptides
suggestions.description: Collagen peptides may improve skin hydration and elasticity (Batool 2026).

references.label: Batool 2026 – Oral collagen peptides & skin: meta-analysis (J Cosmet Dermatol)

suggestions.title: Lutein and zeaxanthin
suggestions.description: Lutein and zeaxanthin are the pigments of the macula, the part of the eye that sees fine detail. Trials show supplements raise macular pigment density. In the AREDS trial, a formula containing beta-carotene slowed the progression of macular degeneration. In AREDS2, lutein and zeaxanthin worked as well as beta-carotene, without beta-carotene's lung cancer signal in former smokers.

references.label: Wilson 2021 – Lutein/zeaxanthin intake & macular pigment optical density: meta-analysis (Adv Nutr)
AREDS 2001 – Vitamins C and E, beta-carotene and zinc for age-related macular degeneration: AREDS Report 8 (Arch Ophthalmol)
AREDS2 2013 – Lutein + zeaxanthin and omega-3 fatty acids for age-related macular degeneration (JAMA)
AREDS2 Report 28, 2022 – Long-term outcomes of lutein/zeaxanthin vs beta-carotene, including lung cancer (JAMA Ophthalmol)

suggestions.title: TMG (trimethylglycine)
suggestions.description: TMG lowers blood homocysteine, according to a meta-analysis of randomized trials. Small trials suggest it may improve strength and power.

references.label: McRae 2013 – Betaine supplementation decreases plasma homocysteine: meta-analysis (J Chiropr Med)
Lee 2010 – Betaine supplementation and strength and power performance (J Int Soc Sports Nutr)
Pryor 2012 – Betaine supplementation and cycling sprint performance (J Int Soc Sports Nutr)
Nobari 2021 – Chronic betaine supplementation in young soccer players: RCT (J Int Soc Sports Nutr)

suggestions.title: Omega-3
suggestions.description: A meta-analysis found omega-3 (EPA/DHA) reduces cardiovascular events and cardiac death. Dr Stanfield thinks it is reasonable for everyone to consider up to 1 g a day of EPA and DHA combined; atrial fibrillation risk rises slightly at that dose and more above it. If you have atrial fibrillation or take a blood thinner, check with your doctor first. In one trial (VITACOG), B vitamins slowed brain atrophy only with good omega-3 levels; another (FACIT) found the reverse. WHO's 2026 guideline recommends against omega-3 supplements to reduce the risk of cognitive decline and dementia in people without a diagnosed deficiency, a strong recommendation based on moderate-certainty evidence. It did not consider the omega-3 analyses of VITACOG or FACIT. It does not address omega-3 for heart health.

references.label: Bernasconi 2021 – Omega-3 dose & cardiovascular outcomes (Mayo Clin Proc)
Gencer 2021 – Omega-3 dose & atrial fibrillation: meta-analysis of RCTs (Circulation)
Jernerén 2015 – B vitamins + omega-3 slow brain atrophy (Am J Clin Nutr)
Oulhaj 2016 – Omega-3 enhances B vitamin cognitive protection (J Alzheimers Dis)
van Soest 2021 – Folic acid & cognition by omega-3 status: FACIT trial (Am J Clin Nutr)
WHO 2026 – Risk reduction of cognitive decline and dementia: guidelines, 2nd edition

suggestions.title: Sleep support
suggestions.description: An umbrella review of meta-analyses found melatonin may reduce the time taken to fall asleep and may improve sleep quality, with a good safety profile — useful as part of a good sleep-hygiene routine.

references.label: Low 2020 – Melatonin efficacy for insomnia (J Psychiatr Res)
Cruz-Sanabria 2024 – Melatonin timing and dose: dose-response meta-analysis (J Pineal Res)

suggestions.title: Daily moisturizer with ceramides
suggestions.description: Use a moisturizer containing ceramides and nicotinamide (vitamin B3) daily. Ceramides restore the skin barrier and reduce wrinkles, while nicotinamide improves hydration and reduces pigmentation.
suggestions.reason: Ceramides are the primary lipids in the skin barrier — a randomised trial showed ceramide-containing moisturisers significantly improved skin hydration and barrier function for up to 7 days. Niacinamide (vitamin B3) is a well-studied ingredient that reduces pigmentation, improves skin texture, and enhances the skin barrier.

references.label: Lueangarun 2019 – Ceramide moisturiser efficacy (Dermatol Ther)
Hakozaki 2002 – Niacinamide reduces pigmentation (Br J Dermatol)

suggestions.title: Daily broad-spectrum sunscreen
suggestions.description: Apply broad-spectrum SPF 50+ sunscreen daily to exposed skin. Beauty of Joseon Relief Sun SPF50+ PA++++ uses newer-generation chemical filters (Tinosorb S, Uvinul A Plus) that are photostable and do not absorb into the bloodstream.
suggestions.reason: A landmark randomised trial (Hughes 2013) proved that daily sunscreen use prevents skin aging — not just sunburn, but the wrinkles, texture changes, and pigmentation caused by UV exposure. Daily broad-spectrum SPF 50+ sunscreen applied to exposed skin is one of the most evidence-backed anti-aging interventions available.

references.label: Hughes 2013 – Sunscreen prevents skin aging: randomised trial (Ann Intern Med)
Randhawa 2016 – Daily sunscreen improves photoaging (Dermatol Surg)

suggestions.title: Topical retinoid
suggestions.description: A topical retinoid (adapalene 0.3% or tretinoin 0.05%) applied at night stimulates collagen production and improves skin texture. Start with 2–3 nights per week and increase as tolerated. Always use sunscreen when using retinoids. Caution: retinoids must not be used during pregnancy.
suggestions.reason: Retinoids (vitamin A derivatives) are the most studied topical anti-aging treatment. They stimulate collagen production, accelerate cell turnover, and improve skin texture. A randomised trial found adapalene 0.3% comparable in efficacy to tretinoin 0.05% for treating photoaging, with better tolerability. Caution: retinoids must not be used during pregnancy.

references.label: Bagatin 2018 – Adapalene vs tretinoin for photoaging (Eur J Dermatol)
Zasada 2019 – Retinoids in skin treatments (Postepy Dermatol Alergol)

suggestions.title: Advanced skin treatments
suggestions.description: For further skin rejuvenation, consider discussing these options with a dermatologist: red light therapy (LED, 630–850nm), fractional laser resurfacing, intense pulsed light (IPL) for pigmentation, and microneedling for collagen induction.
suggestions.reason: For those seeking additional skin rejuvenation, several evidence-based professional treatments exist. Red light therapy (630–850nm) was shown in a controlled trial to significantly reduce wrinkles and increase collagen density. Resistance training has also been shown to improve dermal structure. Other professional options include fractional laser, IPL, and microneedling.

references.label: Wunsch 2014 – Red light therapy for skin rejuvenation (Photomed Laser Surg)
Nishikori 2023 – Resistance training rejuvenates skin (Sci Rep)

suggestions.description: Fat around the middle raises heart and metabolic risk, even at a healthy weight. Aim for a waist under half your height. Add your waist measurement.

suggestions.title: Measure your blood pressure

High blood pressure usually causes no symptoms, so a reading is the only way to know. Home readings with an automated upper-arm cuff, taken seated after a few minutes of rest, are a practical way to track it; every 2–4 weeks is enough to see a trend.

This plan aims for <120/80 mmHg, as some doctors do, based on the SPRINT and ESPRIT trials, or <130/80 mmHg if you're frail.

suggestions.description: Based on your ideal body weight of 60.0 kg, aim for 72g of protein daily. This supports muscle maintenance and metabolic health.

suggestions.description: Aim for 25-35g of fiber daily from whole grains, fruits, and vegetables. Increase gradually to avoid discomfort. If you have IBS or IBD, discuss appropriate fiber levels with your doctor.
suggestions.reason: Dietary fibre may lower cardiovascular risk through several mechanisms: reducing cholesterol absorption, improving blood sugar control, and supporting a healthy gut microbiome. Large cohort studies link the highest fibre intakes with roughly 15–30% lower rates of heart disease, stroke and death than the lowest, and trials show fibre lowers cholesterol and blood pressure.

suggestions.title: Foods that lower cholesterol
suggestions.description: Specific foods can lower LDL cholesterol: oats, walnuts, almonds, ground flaxseed, edamame, and replacing butter with extra-virgin olive oil. If you don't have IBS or IBD, beans, lentils, chickpeas, and mixed vegetables are also great options. Psyllium husk is a soluble fibre that is well-tolerated even with IBS or IBD; discuss with your doctor whether it fits your routine.
suggestions.reason: These foods lower LDL cholesterol through complementary mechanisms: beta-glucan (oats) and soluble fibre (psyllium, flaxseed) bind bile acids, reducing cholesterol reabsorption. Nuts (walnuts, almonds) provide unsaturated fats that improve the LDL-to-HDL ratio. Replacing saturated fat (butter) with monounsaturated fat (extra-virgin olive oil) directly lowers LDL. Soy protein (edamame) modestly reduces LDL when replacing animal protein. Combined, these dietary changes can reduce LDL cholesterol by 15–25%.

suggestions.description: Aim for at least 150 minutes of moderate cardio, or 75 vigorous, or a mix (vigorous minutes count double), plus 2-3 resistance training sessions per week. This combination supports cardiovascular health, muscle mass, and metabolic function.
suggestions.reason: The World Health Organization (2020) and the Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans recommend at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity, or at least 75 minutes of vigorous activity, or a mix of the two (each vigorous minute counts as about two moderate minutes), plus muscle-strengthening activity on 2 or more days a week. suggestions.description: With a BMI of 25.2 and elevated blood pressure, you may benefit from discussing Tirzepatide (preferred) or Semaglutide with your doctor, alongside diet, exercise and sleep. These medications support weight management and metabolic health.
suggestions.reason:
GLP-1 receptor agonists like tirzepatide and semaglutide have been shown in large randomised trials to produce significant, sustained weight loss alongside improvements in blood sugar, blood pressure, and triglycerides. Tirzepatide is preferred due to its dual GIP/GLP-1 mechanism, which may provide greater weight loss. These medications work best alongside diet, exercise, and sleep optimisation.

This plan suggests discussing them at a BMI of 30 or more, above 28 unless your waist is in the healthy range, and from 25 when a marker is raised: HbA1c, blood pressure, triglycerides, cholesterol or waist size. suggestions.title: Consider adding Ezetimibe
suggestions.description: Your LDL-c is 3.6 mmol/L; the treatment target is below 1.4 mmol/L. Discuss adding Ezetimibe 10mg with your doctor. If you are planning a pregnancy, NICE advises stopping 3 months before trying to conceive.
suggestions.reason:
Ezetimibe works differently from statins — it blocks cholesterol absorption in the intestine. Adding ezetimibe to a statin typically lowers LDL by an additional 15–20%. suggestions.description: Aim for less than 1,500mg of sodium daily. Most excess sodium comes from processed foods. Reducing sodium can help lower blood pressure. A potassium-enriched salt substitute can also help cut sodium, but not if you are pregnant, have kidney disease or diabetes, have been told to limit potassium, or take a potassium-sparing diuretic, a potassium supplement, an ACE inhibitor or an ARB, unless your doctor agrees.
suggestions.reason:
Excess sodium raises blood pressure by increasing fluid retention. The ACC/AHA guidelines recommend an ideal sodium intake of less than 1,500mg per day for most adults. Meta-analyses confirm that reducing sodium intake produces meaningful blood pressure reductions, with greater benefit in those who already have elevated blood pressure.

A potassium-enriched salt substitute (75% sodium chloride, 25% potassium chloride) lowered stroke, major cardiovascular events and death in the SSaSS trial, in people in rural China with a past stroke or older adults with high blood pressure. The 2025 AHA/ACC guideline says these substitutes can be useful, except in kidney disease or with medicines that reduce potassium excretion. NICE advises against them for people with diabetes and pregnant women too. So the plan says not to use one if you are pregnant, have kidney disease or diabetes, have been told to limit potassium, or take a potassium-sparing diuretic, a potassium supplement, an ACE inhibitor or an ARB, unless your doctor agrees, and shows the suggestion only with a current eGFR of 45 or more. NICE also advises against them for older people.

suggestions.title: Maximize fiber intake
suggestions.description: Aim for 25-35g of fiber daily from whole grains, fruits, and vegetables. Increase gradually to avoid discomfort. If you have IBS or IBD, discuss appropriate fiber levels with your doctor.
suggestions.reason: Dietary fibre may lower cardiovascular risk through several mechanisms: reducing cholesterol absorption, improving blood sugar control, and supporting a healthy gut microbiome. Large cohort studies link the highest fibre intakes with roughly 15–30% lower rates of heart disease, stroke and death than the lowest, and trials show fibre lowers cholesterol and blood pressure.

suggestions.title: Increase potassium-rich foods
suggestions.description: Aim for 3,500–5,000mg of potassium daily from fruits, vegetables, and legumes. High potassium intake supports healthy blood pressure and cardiovascular function.
suggestions.reason: Potassium helps counteract the blood-pressure-raising effects of sodium. The ISH recommends 3,500–5,000mg/day from food sources. This recommendation only applies when kidney function is adequate (eGFR ≥45), as impaired kidneys may not excrete excess potassium safely.

suggestions.title: Foods that lower cholesterol
suggestions.description: Specific foods can lower LDL cholesterol: oats, walnuts, almonds, ground flaxseed, edamame, and replacing butter with extra-virgin olive oil. If you don't have IBS or IBD, beans, lentils, chickpeas, and mixed vegetables are also great options. Psyllium husk is a soluble fibre that is well-tolerated even with IBS or IBD; discuss with your doctor whether it fits your routine.
suggestions.reason: These foods lower LDL cholesterol through complementary mechanisms: beta-glucan (oats) and soluble fibre (psyllium, flaxseed) bind bile acids, reducing cholesterol reabsorption. Nuts (walnuts, almonds) provide unsaturated fats that improve the LDL-to-HDL ratio. Replacing saturated fat (butter) with monounsaturated fat (extra-virgin olive oil) directly lowers LDL. Soy protein (edamame) modestly reduces LDL when replacing animal protein. Combined, these dietary changes can reduce LDL cholesterol by 15–25%.

Sabaté 2010 – Nut consumption and blood lipid levels (Arch Intern Med)
Wei 2009 – Psyllium fibre lowers cholesterol: meta-analysis (Eur J Clin Nutr)

suggestions.title: Reduce triglycerides with diet
suggestions.description: Blood triglycerides are very diet-sensitive—improvements can be seen within 2-3 weeks. Key measures: limit alcohol, reduce sugar intake, and reduce total fat and calorie intake.
suggestions.reason: Blood triglycerides are highly responsive to dietary changes — improvements can be seen within 2–3 weeks. The most effective dietary measures are reducing sugar and total calorie intake, and reducing alcohol for people who drink. Mendelian randomisation studies confirm that triglyceride-lowering reduces coronary heart disease risk.

references.label: Ference 2019 – Triglyceride-lowering & coronary risk: Mendelian randomisation (JAMA)

suggestions.title: Reduce alcohol intake
suggestions.description: Reduce and ideally completely stop alcohol intake. Alcohol contributes to weight gain, elevated triglycerides, and increased blood pressure.
suggestions.reason: Alcohol contributes to weight gain (7 calories per gram), raises triglycerides, and elevates blood pressure. The International Society of Hypertension recommends reducing or eliminating alcohol intake for blood pressure management and metabolic health.

references.label: Charchar 2023 – ISH lifestyle management of hypertension

suggestions.title: Regular cardio and resistance training
suggestions.description: Aim for at least 150 minutes of moderate cardio, or 75 vigorous, or a mix (vigorous minutes count double), plus 2-3 resistance training sessions per week. This combination supports cardiovascular health, muscle mass, and metabolic function.
suggestions.reason: The World Health Organization (2020) and the Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans recommend at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity, or at least 75 minutes of vigorous activity, or a mix of the two (each vigorous minute counts as about two moderate minutes), plus muscle-strengthening activity on 2 or more days a week. Large studies (PURE, 130,000 people across 17 countries) show that higher physical activity reduces all-cause mortality regardless of income level or country. Cardiorespiratory fitness is one of the strongest predictors of how long people live.

suggestions.title: Prioritize quality sleep
suggestions.description: Aim for 7-9 hours of sleep per night. Maintain a consistent sleep schedule, limit screens before bed, and keep your bedroom cool and dark.
suggestions.reason: Consistent sleep of 7–9 hours per night is essential for cardiovascular health, immune function, and cognitive performance. A large meta-analysis of over 1.3 million participants found that both short sleep (<6 hours) and long sleep (>8–9 hours) are associated with significantly increased mortality risk.

references.label: Cappuccio 2010 – Sleep duration & all-cause mortality: meta-analysis (Sleep)

suggestions.title: Consider a GLP-1 medication
suggestions.description: With a BMI of 27.2 and prediabetic HbA1c, elevated triglycerides, elevated blood pressure and elevated waist-to-height ratio, you may benefit from discussing Tirzepatide (preferred) or Semaglutide with your doctor, alongside diet, exercise and sleep. These medications support weight management and metabolic health.
suggestions.reason:
GLP-1 receptor agonists like tirzepatide and semaglutide have been shown in large randomised trials to produce significant, sustained weight loss alongside improvements in blood sugar, blood pressure, and triglycerides. Tirzepatide is preferred due to its dual GIP/GLP-1 mechanism, which may provide greater weight loss. These medications work best alongside diet, exercise, and sleep optimisation.

This plan raises these medications earlier than guidelines do. Guidelines consider them at a BMI above 30, or above 27 with a weight-related condition, after 3–6 months of lifestyle change. This plan suggests discussing them at a BMI of 30 or more, above 28 unless your waist is in the healthy range, and from 25 when a marker is raised: HbA1c, blood pressure, triglycerides, cholesterol or waist size. No guideline supports these lower BMI thresholds, and a doctor may not agree to prescribe below the licensed ones. The cholesterol lines (ApoB 130 mg/dL, LDL-C 160 mg/dL, non-HDL-C 190 mg/dL or more) are the risk-enhancing levels in the 2018 AHA/ACC cholesterol guideline, which uses them to guide statin decisions, not weight medication.

references.label: Wilding 2021 – Semaglutide for overweight/obesity: STEP 1 trial (NEJM)
Wilding 2022 – Weight regain after semaglutide withdrawal (Diabetes Obes Metab)
Grundy 2018 – AHA/ACC cholesterol guideline: risk-enhancing factors (Circulation)

suggestions.title: HbA1c indicates prediabetes
suggestions.description: Your HbA1c of 6.2 % is in the prediabetic range. Lifestyle changes now can prevent progression to diabetes.
suggestions.reason: An HbA1c in the prediabetic range (5.7–6.4% / 38.8–47.4 mmol/mol) means your blood sugar is higher than normal but not yet diabetic. This is a critical window — lifestyle changes at this stage can prevent or significantly delay progression to type 2 diabetes.

suggestions.title: Elevated Lp(a): 180 nmol/L
suggestions.description:
Lp(a) is genetically determined and cannot be changed by diet or lifestyle. With an elevated Lp(a), reducing all other modifiable cardiovascular risk factors is especially important.

Your modifiable risk factors:
⚠️ ApoB: 120 mg/dL — target <50 mg/dL
⚠️ Blood pressure: 138/86 mmHg — target <120/80
⚠️ BMI: 27.2 — target <25, or <30 with a healthy waist-to-height ratio
⚠️ HbA1c: 6.2 % — target <5.7 %
✅ Statin: Atorvastatin 20mg
⚠️ Ezetimibe: not started — discuss with your doctor
⚠️ PCSK9 inhibitor: not started — can lower Lp(a) ~25–30%
suggestions.reason: Lp(a) is genetically determined — you are born with a set level that cannot be changed through diet or lifestyle. The 2026 ACC/AHA Dyslipidemia Guideline recommends measuring Lp(a) at least once in all adults (Class I). Elevated Lp(a) is an independent cardiovascular risk factor. Since Lp(a) itself cannot be lowered (yet), the strategy is to aggressively reduce all other modifiable risk factors: lipids, blood pressure, blood sugar, weight, and medications where indicated.

references.label: 2026 ACC/AHA Dyslipidemia Guideline (JACC)
Kronenberg 2022 – Lp(a) in cardiovascular disease: EAS consensus (Eur Heart J)

suggestions.title: Low HDL cholesterol
suggestions.description: Your HDL of 39 mg/dL is below optimal (40 mg/dL for men). Exercise and healthy fats can help raise HDL.
suggestions.reason: Low HDL cholesterol is associated with increased cardiovascular risk. Unlike LDL, HDL is generally considered protective — it helps remove cholesterol from arteries. Regular exercise and healthy fats (olive oil, nuts, avocado) can help raise HDL levels. Weight loss also improves HDL.

references.label: 2026 ACC/AHA Dyslipidemia Guideline (JACC)

suggestions.title: Stage 1 hypertension
suggestions.description:
Your BP of 138/86 mmHg indicates stage 1 hypertension. Target is <120/80.

Key lifestyle measures: reduce sodium intake (<1,500mg/day), exercise regularly (150+ min/week), and prioritize quality sleep (7-9 hours).

Increase potassium-rich foods (3,500–5,000mg/day).

Weight loss is one of the most effective ways to lower blood pressure. Even a 5% reduction can make a meaningful difference. GLP-1 medications (tirzepatide, semaglutide) can assist with both weight loss and blood pressure reduction.
suggestions.reason:
Stage 1 hypertension (130–139 systolic or 80–89 diastolic mmHg) is the point at which blood pressure starts to cause meaningful cardiovascular damage over time. Lifestyle measures are the first-line treatment: reduce sodium, increase potassium-rich foods, exercise regularly, prioritise sleep, and manage weight.

Some doctors target <120/80 mmHg for adults under 65. The SPRINT trial showed that targeting <120 mmHg (vs <140 mmHg) reduced cardiovascular events by 25% and all-cause mortality by 27%. The ESPRIT trial extended these findings to a broader population including those with diabetes.

suggestions.title: Consider adding Ezetimibe
suggestions.description: Your ApoB is 120 mg/dL; the treatment target is below 50 mg/dL. Discuss adding Ezetimibe 10mg with your doctor. Not studied enough in pregnancy: talk to your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to be. If you become pregnant, most people should stop their statin: talk to your doctor. If you are planning a pregnancy, NICE advises stopping 3 months before trying to conceive.
suggestions.reason:
Ezetimibe works differently from statins — it blocks cholesterol absorption in the intestine. Adding ezetimibe to a statin typically lowers LDL by an additional 15–20%. Recent evidence shows that starting ezetimibe early alongside a statin produces better cardiovascular outcomes than adding it later.

If a statin is not tolerated, this plan suggests a PCSK9 inhibitor first, because the outcome evidence for ezetimibe on its own is limited, and ezetimibe after it if your level is still above target.

Its US label says there are not enough data on ezetimibe in pregnancy to judge the risk.

suggestions.title: Start colorectal cancer screening
suggestions.description: Colorectal screening is recommended. From 55, Dr Brad suggests a colonoscopy every 10 years. A FIT test every year is also a good option (American Cancer Society). Discuss with your doctor.
suggestions.reason: Dr Brad recommends starting colorectal screening at age 35, because colorectal cancer in adults under 50 has become more common in many countries since the mid-1990s. This is his recommendation, not the official guideline: the American Cancer Society recommends starting at 45 for people at average risk and continuing through 75. Dr Brad suggests a stool test (FIT) every year until 55, then a colonoscopy every 10 years. This order is his suggestion; the American Cancer Society lists FIT every year and colonoscopy every 10 years, among other tests, as equal options from 45. After a positive test and a colonoscopy, follow the repeat interval in your colonoscopy report, which depends on what was found; if the report gave none, Dr Brad suggests repeating the colonoscopy every 3 years. This default is his recommendation, not a guideline figure.

suggestions.title: Discuss prostate cancer screening
suggestions.description: PSA testing is an option after an informed discussion with your doctor. Benefits and risks vary by individual.
suggestions.reason: Prostate cancer screening via PSA testing is a shared decision between patient and doctor. The benefits (early detection) must be weighed against the risks (overdiagnosis and overtreatment of slow-growing cancers). Long-term follow-up of the Prostate Cancer Prevention Trial showed that 5-alpha reductase inhibitors can reduce prostate cancer incidence.

suggestions.title: Micronutrient base
suggestions.description: A meta-analysis of three COSMOS trial sub-studies (2024) found that a daily multivitamin improved global cognition and episodic memory in older adults. This suggests broad micronutrient support may benefit brain health alongside filling common dietary gaps. The WHO's 2026 dementia guideline recommends against vitamin B, vitamin E, omega-3 and multivitamin-mineral supplements to reduce the risk of cognitive decline and dementia in people without a diagnosed deficiency, a strong recommendation based on moderate-certainty evidence. It kept its earlier recommendation without reassessing supplements, and did not cite the COSMOS trials. If you take warfarin (Coumadin, Marevan) or another vitamin K antagonist, check with your doctor or anticoagulation clinic before starting or stopping vitamin K2, because it can change your INR.

suggestions.description: One of the most-studied supplements: a meta-analysis found creatine (3–5 g/day) significantly increases muscle strength and lean mass with resistance training. There is also an interesting signal that it may help memory, another possible benefit; formal reviews are mixed, with the clearest benefit in older adults.

suggestions.description: Lutein and zeaxanthin are the pigments of the macula, the part of the eye that sees fine detail. Trials show supplements raise macular pigment density. In the AREDS trial, a formula containing beta-carotene slowed the progression of macular degeneration. In AREDS2, lutein and zeaxanthin worked as well as beta-carotene, without beta-carotene's lung cancer signal in former smokers.

suggestions.title: Omega-3
suggestions.description: A meta-analysis found omega-3 (EPA/DHA) reduces cardiovascular events and cardiac death. Dr Stanfield thinks it is reasonable for everyone to consider up to 1 g a day of EPA and DHA combined; atrial fibrillation risk rises slightly at that dose and more above it. If you have atrial fibrillation or take a blood thinner, check with your doctor first. In one trial (VITACOG), B vitamins slowed brain atrophy only with good omega-3 levels; another (FACIT) found the reverse. WHO's 2026 guideline recommends against omega-3 supplements to reduce the risk of cognitive decline and dementia in people without a diagnosed deficiency, a strong recommendation based on moderate-certainty evidence. It did not consider the omega-3 analyses of VITACOG or FACIT. It does not address omega-3 for heart health.

suggestions.title: Sleep support
suggestions.description: An umbrella review of meta-analyses found melatonin may reduce the time taken to fall asleep and may improve sleep quality, with a good safety profile — useful as part of a good sleep-hygiene routine.

suggestions.title: Daily moisturizer with ceramides
suggestions.description: Use a moisturizer containing ceramides and nicotinamide (vitamin B3) daily. Ceramides restore the skin barrier and reduce wrinkles, while nicotinamide improves hydration and reduces pigmentation.
suggestions.reason: Ceramides are the primary lipids in the skin barrier — a randomised trial showed ceramide-containing moisturisers significantly improved skin hydration and barrier function for up to 7 days. Niacinamide (vitamin B3) is a well-studied ingredient that reduces pigmentation, improves skin texture, and enhances the skin barrier.

references.label: Lueangarun 2019 – Ceramide moisturiser efficacy (Dermatol Ther)
Hakozaki 2002 – Niacinamide reduces pigmentation (Br J Dermatol)

suggestions.title: Daily broad-spectrum sunscreen
suggestions.description: Apply broad-spectrum SPF 50+ sunscreen daily to exposed skin. In the US, CeraVe 100% Mineral Sunscreen SPF 50 is a good option — mineral filters (zinc oxide, titanium dioxide) are FDA-recognized as safe and effective with no systemic absorption.
suggestions.reason: A landmark randomised trial (Hughes 2013) proved that daily sunscreen use prevents skin aging — not just sunburn, but the wrinkles, texture changes, and pigmentation caused by UV exposure. Daily broad-spectrum SPF 50+ sunscreen applied to exposed skin is one of the most evidence-backed anti-aging interventions available.

references.label: Hughes 2013 – Sunscreen prevents skin aging: randomised trial (Ann Intern Med)
Randhawa 2016 – Daily sunscreen improves photoaging (Dermatol Surg)

suggestions.title: Topical retinoid
suggestions.description: A topical retinoid (adapalene 0.3% or tretinoin 0.05%) applied at night stimulates collagen production and improves skin texture. Start with 2–3 nights per week and increase as tolerated. Always use sunscreen when using retinoids. Caution: retinoids must not be used during pregnancy.
suggestions.reason: Retinoids (vitamin A derivatives) are the most studied topical anti-aging treatment. They stimulate collagen production, accelerate cell turnover, and improve skin texture. A randomised trial found adapalene 0.3% comparable in efficacy to tretinoin 0.05% for treating photoaging, with better tolerability. Caution: retinoids must not be used during pregnancy.

references.label: Bagatin 2018 – Adapalene vs tretinoin for photoaging (Eur J Dermatol)

suggestions.title: Advanced skin treatments
suggestions.description: For further skin rejuvenation, consider discussing these options with a dermatologist: red light therapy (LED, 630–850nm), fractional laser resurfacing, intense pulsed light (IPL) for pigmentation, and microneedling for collagen induction.
suggestions.reason: For those seeking additional skin rejuvenation, several evidence-based professional treatments exist. Red light therapy (630–850nm) was shown in a controlled trial to significantly reduce wrinkles and increase collagen density. Resistance training has also been shown to improve dermal structure. Other professional options include fractional laser, IPL, and microneedling.
